papers.title: Human Centric Embodied Intelligence for Soft Wearable Robotics
papers.summary: Soft wearable robots have evolved rapidly from proof‐of‐concept devices into promising platforms for rehabilitation, occupational assistance, and human augmentation. As the field matures, its central challenge extends beyond developing softer materials and more capable actuators to integrating sensing, intelligence, and human adaptation into systems that users can wear comfortably, trust, and benefit from over long periods. papers.title: Sound2Vision: Generating Diverse Visuals from Audio through Cross-Modal Latent Alignment
papers.summary: How does audio describe the world around us? In this work, we propose a method for generating images of visual scenes from diverse in-the-wild sounds. This cross-modal generation task is challenging due to the significant information gap between auditory and visual signals. We address this challenge by designing a model that aligns audio-visual modalities by enriching audio features with visual information and translating them into the visual latent space. papers.title: Recent advances in multi-agent human trajectory prediction: A comprehensive review
papers.summary: With the emergence of powerful data-driven methods in human trajectory prediction (HTP), gaining a finer understanding of multi-agent interactions lies within hand’s reach, with important implications in areas such as social robot navigation, autonomous driving, and crowd modeling. This survey reviews some of the most recent advancements in deep learning-based multi-agent trajectory prediction, focusing on studies published between 2020 and 2025. Fishers reward program promoting their role as cleaners of the ocean
papers.summary: Marine litter poses an environmental and socio-economic challenge in European seas, imposing costs on fishers who passively collect waste during routine operations. This study explores reward-based programs to incentivise coastal fishers to collect marine litter, drawing on qualitative evidence from Croatia, Italy, Malta, Portugal, and Spain. The study contributes to the debate on recognising fisheries for their environmental contribution beyond seafood production, framing marine litter removal as a public environmental good requiring policy support. papers.title: EASQ: Energy-Aware Container Scheduling with Tabular Q-Learning for Orchestrated Cloud Clusters
papers.summary: Default container schedulers place workloads using rules fixed at deployment time: Docker Swarm’s spread strategy equalises container counts across nodes, and Kubernetes’s bin-packing (MostAllocated) scoring profile packs them by requested—not consumed—resources. Both ignore what a placement costs in watts. We formulate container placement as a Markov decision process and train a tabular Q-learning agent, EASQ, whose shaped reward charges each placement its marginal power increase while penalising utilisation beyond a safety threshold. papers.summary: This study examines how task framing influences personality-based team selection decisions. We will analyze whether framing systematically shifts which personality traits people prioritize when selecting teammates, and whether this produces differences in team diversity. papers.summary: The integration of the arts with science, technology, engineering, and mathematics increasingly defines the content of modern school education; however, the artistic component in STEAM projects is often reduced to mere decoration of a technical product. papers.title: TEACHERS’ ATTITUDES AND RESPONSES TO BULLYING AT SCHOOL
papers.summary: Bullying is a form of intentional, repeated aggressive behavior aimed at causing physical, psychological or emotional harm to an individual perceived as weaker or disadvantaged. It occurs when there is an imbalance of power between the perpetrator and the victim, with the former using physical force, intimidation, insults or other forms of manipulation to exercise control or hurt the other person.
